Done. `index.html` edited in place, still one file, still auto-plays the default crash, CDN Three r165 + Rapier 0.14.

## Per-frame cost cuts

**Rendering**
- Post stack removed entirely (EffectComposer, SSAO, bloom, OutputPass). Frame is now 2 scene passes (shadow + beauty) instead of ~4 scene renders + SSAO blur + 5 bloom mips. ACES tone mapping stays on the renderer.
- Contact shadows kept, re-implemented as one instanced draw of soft occlusion blobs under every car part and brick (alpha/size driven by gap to ground; ~90 visible at rest, ~215 after the collapse). Wall base, wheels and fallen bricks stay grounded.
- Glass: transmission dropped (it re-renders the whole scene per frame) → alpha-blended `MeshPhysicalMaterial` with strong env reflections, one material shared by panes and shards.
- Draw calls ~140 → **51–56**. Each rigid body's sub-meshes are baked and merged per material (`flattenGroup`), wheels are 2 draws instead of 9, static environment is merged into 9 draws (rails, curbs, gravel, 4 poles+arms, lamps, posts as one InstancedMesh).
- Shadows: 4096 → 2048 map, PCFSoft kept (spec asks for soft PCF; cost ≈ PCF). Frustum is re-fitted every frame around the wall + wherever the parts are. Casters: only car parts, bricks, shards (~40 vs ~130); no environment casters.
- Lights: hemisphere removed, sun + env map only. Bump maps off on asphalt/gravel. Pixel ratio cap 1.5 → 1.25, aniso 4, sky dome 24×12, particle pools 900/420 → 520/260, skid cap 400, shards/skids only draw live instances, HUD DOM writes throttled to ~12 Hz.

**Physics**
- Solver iterations 8 → 4 (default), CCD off on 200 bricks, shards and wheels (kept on the fast car panels so nothing tunnels), contact-force events only on car colliders (brick↔brick / brick↔ground pairs are event-free; brick landing puffs come from a 12-bricks-per-step round-robin scan), shards ≤64 with coarser grids, sleeping bricks skip matrix updates, physics step cap 6 → 4.

## Things I had to fix to make it "complete" (flagging because they change the crash)

Running the module headless in Node (real Rapier, stubbed WebGL, no browser) showed the pre-pass version never worked: all 29 joints broke during the *approach* (solver jitter vs 3–5 g thresholds + a 27 kN wheel spike), and at the wall the whole car disintegrated to a bare tub. Fixes:
- Drive force applied per part ∝ mass (joints carry no drivetrain load), small lane/heading hold, joints armed only after first wall contact.
- Wheel colliders `cylinder` → `roundCylinder`: sharp cylinders sliding at 20 m/s chattered and lifted the rear axle 18 cm (40 cm with 8 iterations).
- Break rule: inertial load low-passed (~30 ms), direct-hit force taken on the attached part only, ground slams excluded. Engine bay–cabin is now unibody (unbreakable); front wheels/door hinges tear off from direct hits at 12/15 kN.
- Detached wheels/panels get rolling resistance so the scene settles (~11 s instead of the 14 s fallback); paved run-off extended past the wall since 1250 kg at 22 m/s keeps ~18 m/s through a 500 kg loose wall and the wreck stops ~17 m past it; impact camera dollies with it.

Measured outcome: impact at t=2.258 s (identical across replays and frame pacing), 193/200 bricks displaced, front bumper/nose/hood/fenders/engine/both front wheels/all glass off, doors popped (two torn off), rear intact and recognizable. 12 kg bricks or 12 m/s give clearly different outcomes.
